title: Robot-Assisted Progressive Muscle Strength Training Protocol
author: Azeemsha Thacham Poyil
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.5hrg356

steps.title: Measure Participant Baseline Metrics
steps.instruction: Collect baseline physical measurements for all participants.

substeps.instruction: Measure body weight, Body Mass Index (BMI), visceral fat classification, skeletal muscle percentage, and body fat percentage.
Record gender, age, and height.

steps.title: Attach EMG Electrodes
steps.instruction: Fix EMG electrodes on the upper limb muscles and the ground electrode.

substeps.instruction: Place electrodes on the Biceps Brachii (BB), Anterior Deltoid (DLTF), and Middle Deltoid (DLTM).
Connect the ground electrode to a bony area near the elbow.

steps.title: Determine MVC-Equivalent (MVC-Eq)
steps.instruction: Measure the highest feasible robotic resistance for the rowing task to establish the MVC-Eq.

substeps.instruction: Gradually increase robotic resistance by adjusting the damping coefficient of the robotic end-effector until a comfortable highest level is reached, using verbal feedback from the subject.
Note the damping coefficient corresponding to the highest feasible force.
Conduct three such measurements with a break period of at least 30 seconds between each trial.
Calculate the average of the three readings to determine the MVC-Eq.

steps.title: Recovery and Familiarization
steps.instruction: Allow participants to recover and familiarize themselves with the equipment.

substeps.instruction: Provide a break period of 10 minutes or until self-reported full recovery after MVC trials.
Conduct a practice run for participants to familiarize themselves with the robot and environment.

steps.title: Perform Rowing Task (Group-B: Intervention)
steps.instruction: Execute the rowing task using a fatigue-adaptive robotic environment based on EMG features.

substeps.instruction: Start a single continuous trial without break periods.
Increment difficulty level by 10% MVC-Eq every 1 minute.
If the algorithm detects fatigue, automatically decrease the difficulty level to 50% of the current value.
When the subject is relaxed, resume incrementing the robotic resistance by 10% MVC-Eq after a 1-minute trial.
Repeat until the resistance reaches 100% MVC-Eq or the participant reports fatigue 3 times.

steps.title: Perform Rowing Task (Group-A: Control 1)
steps.instruction: Execute the rowing task with regular break periods and no robotic adaptation.

substeps.instruction: Perform each trial for 1 minute or until the participant feels tired.
Provide a break of 30 seconds after each trial.
After the break, increment the robotic resistance by 10% MVC-Eq.
Repeat the 1-minute trial and break cycle until the resistance reaches 100% MVC-Eq or the participant reports fatigue 3 times.

steps.title: Perform Rowing Task (Group-C: Control 2)
steps.instruction: Execute the rowing task using subjective fatigue reports for robotic adaptation.

substeps.instruction: Start a single continuous trial without break periods.
Increment difficulty level by 10% MVC-Eq after every 1-minute trial.
If the participant reports fatigue, decrease the difficulty level to 50% of the current value.
After 1 minute, resume incrementing the robotic resistance by 10% MVC-Eq.
Repeat until the resistance reaches 100% MVC-Eq or the participant reports fatigue 3 times.

steps.title: Log Experimental Data
steps.instruction: Record all relevant parameters during the experiment at a rate of approximately 10 samples per second.

substeps.instruction: Log subject group name, MVC-Equivalent, and number of rowing iterations.
Log kinematic measurements: end-effector position, velocity, and force.
Log muscle fatigue states: reported fatigue, detected fatigue, and relaxed state.
